Description: Edmund Galley and Helen Dauer clash head-on in the Billiard room. The dialogue explicitly reveals for the first time that Helen Dauer has a daughter, and Edmund Galley directly states that she is dead, triggering a violent emotional breakdown and a piercing scream that draws everyone in the villa to the room.
Location: Billiard room (Billiard room)
Key Information:
  - After Edmund Galley enters the Billiard room, he begins playing pool; Helen Dauer enters shortly afterward and confronts him.
  - Helen Dauer accuses Edmund Galley, as host, of negligence for failing to explain the villa’s abnormal situation to the guests.
  - Edmund Galley states for the first time that there are already three corpses in the villa, and claims this is an intimidation tactic carried out by one of the guests.
  - Helen Dauer is furious that Edmund Galley allowed an “outsider” into the villa and demands that he confront the outsider directly.
  - They argue over a ring; Edmund Galley says he has found the ring and is willing to return it.
  - Helen Dauer explicitly mentions for the first time that she has a daughter and demands to know where she is.
  - Edmund Galley says he did not previously know Helen Dauer had a daughter and insists he did not see any stranger enter the villa.
  - Helen Dauer says her daughter had been resting in Edmund Galley’s room and orders him to go check immediately.
  - Edmund Galley states on the spot that Helen Dauer’s daughter is already dead, provoking Helen Dauer’s fierce denial and rage.
  - They escalate into a heated argument over whether a daughter exists, whether anyone was informed earlier, and who is responsible.
  - Helen Dauer loses control, clearly shouts “Stay away from my children,” and threatens him by invoking her son’s gun.
  - The confrontation ends with an extremely loud scream.
  - Shortly after Edmund Galley leaves the Billiard room, everyone else in the villa enters the room one after another.
Characters:
  [Edmund Galley (Edmund Galley)] Person No. 6, the male host of the villa.
    · Tries to be alone in the Billiard room to collect his thoughts.
    · States for the first time that there are already three corpses in the villa.
    · Says he did not previously know Helen Dauer has a daughter.
    · Directly asserts that Helen Dauer’s daughter is dead.
    · Leaves the Billiard room after the conflict escalates.
  [Helen Dauer (Helen Dauer)] Person No. 9, a guest and Tony Dauer’s mother.
    · Shows intense dissatisfaction with Edmund Galley’s negligence and attitude.
    · Repeatedly insists she has a daughter and presses for her whereabouts.
    · Rejects the claim that her daughter is dead and progressively loses emotional control.
    · Clearly shouts “Stay away from my children.”
    · Threatens him by invoking her son’s gun.
    · Screams at the height of the confrontation.
  [Eve Dauer (Eve Dauer)] Person No. 10, Helen Dauer’s daughter, confirmed deceased.
    · Is explicitly identified by Helen Dauer as her daughter.
    · Was previously placed to rest in Edmund Galley’s room.
    · Is directly judged by Edmund Galley in this node to already be dead.
